The 22-matter table may therefore be incomplete, and the agent treated it as complete.

The agent's self-assessment claims a complete per-matter table, but the visible output shows hit counts of 1-3 per matter and a truncated result. Several dates are '-' (1007-00004), so the 'latest' ordering rests on partial evidence.
critique.concerns: The matching was filtered by file name and relied on 'labor and employment' phrases in staff titles. That can mark matters as L&E because an L&E partner appears, as in 1009-00007, which is a transaction with cross-staffing. It can also miss true L&E matters. The agent concedes it has not yet shown which matter contains agreed acceleration terms. The classification is not verified as complete.
critique.recommendation: Do not treat the 22-matter table as complete. Re-scan all .docx files in every matter without filtering by file name, and flag matters whose text shows a Labor & Employment practice group. Then search all matters for acceleration terms and read the executed documents of the matters that hit, newest first by actual date.
